title: Recipe 13 — MCP Servers (tools you didn't write, namespaced and gated)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “MCP is how you get tools you didn't write — a community filesystem server, a Postgres server, someone else's Go binary.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the run beat calls a remote tool, which means calling the model first.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “A plain cli agent — MCP adds tools to it, it doesn't change the shape.”

beats.label: Add the agent block
beats.cue: “The instructions name the prefix, because the prefix is what the model will see.”

beats.label: Wire the reference MCP server
beats.cue: “Five lines: a name, a transport, and the command the runtime spawns. That's the whole integration.”

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing spawned, nothing emitted.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “mcpServers survives lowering verbatim — transport, command, args. The compiler doesn't interpret them; the runtime does.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target cli, mcpServers.everything included

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, no key.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate, which is reached before the MCP handshake

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: “The MCP host is a runtime import, not generated code — the bundle hands it the server table and gets a tool list back.”

groups.title: Beat 3 · Call a tool you didn't write

beats.label: Launch the REPL with MCP debug on
beats.cue: [needs-key] “CREWHAUS_MCP_DEBUG=1 logs every MCP message — the handshake, tools/list, tools/call.”

verify.note: spawns npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything on the way up; the chat loop needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Ask it to use the remote tool
beats.cue: [needs-key] “The model asks for everything__echo — prefixed, because two servers with a `read` tool would otherwise collide.”
beats.text: echo hello using the everything server

verify.note: runtime serializes tools/call over stdio; the response is classified with origin "mcp" before it reaches the model

beats.label: Exit the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell, and the runtime reaps the server subprocess.

groups.title: One more thing · many servers, one spec — and permissions on the prefixed names

beats.label: Blank a second scratch spec
beats.cue: “A production CLI agent runs three to five of these. There's no limit and no shared state.”

beats.label: Same agent, second spec
beats.cue: “Identical head — the interesting part is what we hang off it.”

beats.label: Wire four servers, two transports
beats.cue: “Two stdio subprocesses the runtime spawns, two SSE connections to servers someone else operates.”

beats.label: Gate the remote tools by name
beats.cue: “Permission rules match the prefixed name — same grammar as Read and Bash. read_file allowed, write_file asks, create_repository denied.”

beats.label: Lint the four-server spec
beats.cue: “Clean — and note lint never dials the SSE URLs. Nothing here needs those services to exist.”

verify.note: lint: clean — no findings; sse urls are not resolved at lint time

beats.label: Lower it to IR on disk
beats.cue: “Four servers, and the three permission rules beside them — one JSON object the runtime consumes.”

verify.note: redirect, not a pipe — the exit code is the compiler's

beats.label: Read the lowered server table
beats.cue: “filesystem, git, postgres, sentry — and the model will see filesystem__read_file, github__create_issue, and so on.”
